general_lemma.novelty_boundary: A direct corollary of existing cooperative/Metzler differential comparison, not a proposed new mathematical comparison principle.
general_lemma.proof: w=x-Y satisfies w_prime=M(k)*w-R and w(0)<=0. Apply the already audited metzler_nonpos or differential_comparison theorem with the actual matrix M(k).
general_lemma.proposed_formal_use: differential_comparison M hM x Y (M*x+f) dY; use linear_sub and the residual inequality to discharge its derivative-difference premise.
general_lemma.barrier: Y has an actual displayed derivative dY, and residual R=dY-M(k)*Y-f(k,u(t)) is componentwise nonnegative.
general_lemma.setting: Finite real vector space, fixed parameter k, fixed Metzler matrix M(k), additive forcing f(k,u(t)).
hypotheses_not_needed: No componentwise order between M(k) and the endpoint matrix.
No nonnegativity assumption on the actual state x is needed for this upper comparison.
No nonnegativity assumption on f is needed once the barrier residual is verified.
Y need not be an actual solution to some other parameter model for comparison alone; actual feasibility is needed separately to certify an attained maximum.
general_lemma.regularity: Each component of x,Y is continuous on[0,infinity), and has the displayed classical derivative at every t>0. This is the current Lean comparison contract; no general existence claim for arbitrary measurable inputs is included.

three_tank.gap_02: Y0-Y2=q*(1-q)*(8-q-q^2)/6; alternatively sum the two nonnegative gaps
three_tank.sign_check: For t>=0,0<q<=1. The upper parameter inequalities, nonnegative rates and u<=1 make every displayed residual term nonnegative.
three_tank.source_semantic_verdict: The displayed endpoint_drift_domination and solution_below_endpoint use the actual fixed matrix as the comparison matrix, so they implement the residual argument correctly. No source-level blocking semantic issue found in the read version.
three_tank.barrier_nonnegative: Y2=(1-q)^2*(6-2*q-q^2)/6>=0 for0<=q<=1; Y1,Y0 are also nonnegative.

exact_maximum_scope.not_each_fixed_inlet: The maximum is over the combined parameter and bounded-input family. It does not say the endpoint parameters maximize the output for every preassigned inlet profile u(t).
exact_maximum_scope.feasibility: endpoint_admissible, endpointState_hasDerivAt, endpointState_zero, endpointState_actual_solution and endpointState_attainable supply actual model membership and the witness. A merely synthetic interval matrix would not suffice for attainability.
exact_maximum_scope.optimization_family: All admissible fixed rate tuples, all time-varying input functions satisfying0<=u<=1, and all given classical solutions with zero initial state.
exact_maximum_scope.no_uniqueness_claim: This gives an attaining witness; it does not characterize all maximizing parameters or controls, and is not a uniqueness theorem.
exact_maximum_scope.physical_scope: The coefficient-box theorem does not certify arbitrary hardware uncertainty. The all-upper tuple is compatible with uniformly scaling the nominal ideal flow network by c, but the formal optimization family is the stated coefficient model.
exact_maximum_scope.maximum: For any fixed t>=0 and coordinate i, every such x_i(t)<=Y_i(t), and the single fixed endpoint tuple with the unit input produces the actual trajectory Y. Thus this pair attains the componentwise upper envelope, simultaneously for all t and all coordinates.

no_conflict_with_phase2_counterexample.matrix_order: Increasing a transfer rate simultaneously raises an off-diagonal term and lowers a diagonal term. Positivity alone never supplies componentwise parameter monotonicity.
no_conflict_with_phase2_counterexample.current_barrier: The phase3 upper trajectory uses the constant upper inlet1. Its first residual includes the nonnegative payment k0*(1-u), and its feedforward coordinate gaps remain nonnegative. Therefore it can bound an actual decaying inlet without claiming that the actual upper-rate decaying-inlet solution dominates all other parameters.
no_conflict_with_phase2_counterexample.counterexample: At the same prescribed decaying inlet v(t)=exp(-t), y_prime=k*(v-y), y(0)=0. The fixed-time map k->y_k(log4) is neither increasing nor decreasing.
no_conflict_with_phase2_counterexample.failing_residual: If Y is the actual upper-rate response to that same v, then Y_prime-k*(v-Y)=(k_star-k)*(v-Y). The tracking gap v-Y can be negative after the inlet declines, so endpoint domination has no general sign certificate.

possible_generalizations.candidate: Arbitrary edge-rate families with a known barrier order
possible_generalizations.statement: For F_i=sum_j a_ij*(X_j-X_i)+source/leak terms, it suffices to certify each row residual sum along Y. Products (a_star_ij-a_ij)*(Y_j-Y_i)>=0 are a useful sufficient condition, even when matrix entries are not ordered. Individual nonnegative products are sufficient, not logically necessary: positive/negative terms can also cancel to a nonnegative row sum.

possible_generalizations.candidate: Wider boxes below the same proportional cap
possible_generalizations.statement: For any c>0, the same polynomial barrier proves the same sign argument for0<=k0<=c,0<=k10<=2*c,0<=k20<=c,0<=k21<=3*c. The five-percent lower bounds are used only to imply nonnegative rates; the proportional cap makes the explicit barrier formula available. This is a paper generalization, not added to the current Lean source.

For an arbitrary nonnegative upper tuple, the step-response gaps g=Y0-Y1 and d=Y1-Y2 satisfy g_prime=Y0_prime-k10_star*g and d_prime=(k10_star-k20_star)*g-(k20_star+k21_star)*d. Thus k10_star>=k20_star and the unit-step first coordinate provide another sufficient ordering criterion without the special polynomial formula. This has not been formalized here.

A residual comparison extends mathematically under suitable positive-evolution/quasimonotone hypotheses and appropriate solution regularity. The existing Lean theorem is for a fixed matrix; replacing k by k(t), or asserting arbitrary measurable/Caratheodory solutions, requires a new formal interface and is outside this checked stage.
